To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Esipov-Shapiro model, when solved numer-ically with a method that is known to converge to a solution, does not produce spatial regularity; (2) the spatial regularity seen experimentally can be reproduced in a model that is a natural extension of the Esipov- Shapiro model, and (3) the model that produces spatial regularity can be used to study the effect of various parameters on the dynamics of Proteus swarm-colony development.

the Esipov-Shapiro model, when solved numeri- cally, does not display the spatial regularity seen experimentally, and that a simple modification of the model, with explicit age-structure, can be solved numerically to display both temporal and spatial regularities.

Proteus mirabil is a model biological system for the development of structured population models; the Esipov-Shapiro model of Proteus swarm-colony development is an important contribution to structured population modeling; and the structured-population model developed in this paper, which includes spatial diffusion, is the best model of Proteus swarms available at present.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a model of Proteus swarm-colony development that is based on known aspects of the cell-cycle, and that can be used to study the effect of various assumptions on the spatial dynamics of Proteus colonies.
the development of mathematical and computational models of biological systems and with the application of such models to biological problems.

the development of a mathematical model of the dynamics of a bacterial swarm colony, with a view to using the model as a basis for the design of experiments to test hypotheses about the mechanism of swarm-colony formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Esipov-Shapiro model is not adequate for the description of the spatial regularity of Proteus mirabili swarm-colony development, whereas a model that includes the effects of cell age does provide such a description.
the models and numerical computations in this paper are consistent with the experimental observations, but do not provide a complete explanation of the system.
the models in this paper provide a reasonable representation of the experimental data and that the spatial regularity seen is due to the age-structure of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and tested a model for the development of Proteus mirobilis swarm-colonies, and that the model is consistent with experimental results.

, while we do not understand the spatial mechanisms in Proteus mirabil is swarm-colony development well enough to construct a complete model, we have shown that the Esipov-Shapiro model is a good starting point for a model that can reproduce the experimental results.

the models in this paper, when coupled with the numerical methods, provide an accurate description of Proteus mirobilis swarm-colony dynamics, including the temporal and spatial patterns seen in experiments, and that the numerical results are obtained using methods with known convergence properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the spatial dynamics of Proteus swarm colonies depend on local physiological age-structure, the age-structure is not the primary cause of the spatial dynamics.
the Esipov-Shapiro model can be improved to give a more realistic representation of the spatial dynamics of Proteus swarm colonies.

the age-structured models we present are capable of reproducing the spatial and temporal regularities observed in experiments, and that these regularities are robust to the details of the spatial diffusion mechanism.
